name: IoT Cloud, Backend & OTA Update Security
description: Covers the security of the backend ecosystem behind IoT devices: device provisioning, identity and certificate lifecycle, MQTT and CoAP broker configuration and topic/resource authorisation, companion mobile apps and cloud APIs, and fleet management. Includes over-the-air (OTA) update security: signing and verification, update server and delivery channel integrity, and anti-rollback protection. On-device firmware and interface testing belongs to ICSIOT-IOT-DEVICE; generic web API testing belongs to SWSEC-WEB-API.

0.label: None
0.description: No exposure to IoT backend or OTA update security

1.label: Awareness
1.description: Understands the IoT backend attack surface and why fleet-wide compromise is the key risk
evidence: Can describe the device-to-cloud architecture: provisioning service, broker, APIs, companion app, OTA service
Can explain how MQTT topics and CoAP resources are authorised and why wildcard subscriptions are dangerous
Understands code signing, anti-rollback and why an unsigned OTA channel enables fleet-wide compromise

2.label: Guided Practice
2.description: Tests IoT backend components under supervision
evidence: Tests an MQTT broker for anonymous access, weak credentials and cross-tenant topic access in a lab
Intercepts companion app and device traffic to map the cloud API with guidance
Checks OTA packages for signatures, transport protection and version metadata
Documents findings with the affected device population and ecosystem component

3.label: Independent Practice
3.description: Independently assesses IoT backend, provisioning and OTA security end to end
evidence: Assesses device identity and provisioning: per-device credentials, certificate issuance and revocation, claim/ownership flows
Tests broker and API authorisation for device-to-device and tenant isolation (e.g. IDOR via device identifiers)
Evaluates OTA update signing, verification on device, rollback protection and update server security
Produces reports that tie backend findings to fleet-wide impact and mitigations

4.label: Advanced / Mentor
4.description: Assesses complex IoT platforms; develops tooling; mentors others
evidence: Assesses cloud IoT platform configurations (device policies, rules engines, shadow/twin services) for privilege escalation
Develops tooling for device impersonation, broker fuzzing or OTA manipulation testing
Reviews OTA and key management architecture designs, including signing key protection in HSMs
Mentors staff and calibrates IoT ecosystem assessments across the team

5.label: Expert / Authority
5.description: Defines the lab's IoT ecosystem assessment practice; publishes research
evidence: Established the lab's methodology for IoT backend, provisioning and OTA assessment
Published research on IoT cloud, broker or update-mechanism vulnerabilities
Contributes to industry guidance or standards on IoT update and device identity security
Trains teams on IoT ecosystem security assessment

assessment_methods.description: Given a lab IoT device with a broker, cloud API and companion app, impersonate a device, demonstrate a cross-device authorisation flaw, and evaluate whether a downgraded or tampered OTA image is accepted
Review an IoT ecosystem assessment report for coverage of provisioning, broker authorisation, API and OTA findings and a clear statement of fleet-wide impact
